title: Asymmetric Kernel Fidelity Profiling  Guidelines and Experiment Matrix
author: Asha Patel
summary: This playbook documents a repeatable approach to profile and evaluate asymmetric kernel variants used by the runtime: kernels that offer different fidelity or approximation levels (full-precision, quantized, approx-attention, mixed-kernel offloads). It provides an experiment matrix, instrumentation checklist, and interpretation guidance so kernel rollouts keep application-level quality and SLOs intact.
scope: Applies to runtime kernel families used in production inference (attention, matmul, kv-cache ops). Focuses on profiling permutations where a request may fall back between kernel fidelity levels and on measuring the operational cost of transitions.
goals: Detect fidelity regressions at prompt-set level; quantify latency and p99 tail per-kernel and per-sequence-length; validate graceful fallback behavior and measure reconfiguration costs; provide a go/no-go decision matrix for kernel rollout aligned with SLO thresholds.
definitions: High-fidelity kernel: reference kernel prioritized for output quality (FP16/FP32). Economical kernel: optimized for cost/throughput (quantized, approximate) with potential quality delta. Fallback oscillation: repeated switching between kernels that causes latency spikes or quality divergence.
prerequisites_and_ownership: Owned by eng-serving-runtime (profiling lead) with review from kernel maintainers and SRE. Required infra: profiling cluster with representative GPUs (A100/H100 and a low-cost pool like A10G), workload-replay service, and tracing hooks enabled. Provide access to artifact storage, a dashboard template (Grafana id: runtime.kernel.fidelity.profile), and the applied-ml-evals harness.
instrumentation_checklist: Kernel-level timers per dispatch; request timeline markers (request_receive, model_load, kv_attach, kernel_dispatch(N), kernel_complete(N), response_stream_start); memory copy accounting between device regions; fidelity flag telemetry attached to kernel_dispatch events; quality trace linking prompt_id -> candidate_hash -> golden_eval_id.
sampling_strategy_and_telemetry_budget: Stratified sampling by sequence length cohorts: short (<=64), medium (65-512), long (>512). SLO-aware sampling: increase sample rate during tail events and for high-sensitivity customers. Telemetry cost cap: profiling telemetry should not exceed 6% of production inference compute on the profiling cluster.
experiment_matrix: 1) Baseline characterization: reference kernels only; canonical prompt-set; metrics: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, memory, energy, quality. 2) Single kernel substitution: replace one operator kernel with economical variant; run per cohort and measure quality drift and latency delta. 3) Mixed-mode (fallback) replay: enable runtime fallback policy and inject capacity events; track fallback frequency, transition time, oscillations. 4) Session-boundary stress: simulate long chat sessions to measure cache conversion/regeneration costs. 5) Canary with adversarial corpus: include prompts sensitive to approximation; run human eval gates for semantic regressions.
bench_commands_and_snippets:
replay-runner --corpus dev-corpus-v3 --cohort short,medium,long --kernel-policy ref_only --out results/baseline
replay-runner --corpus dev-corpus-v3 --cohort short,medium,long --kernel-policy economical_attention --out results/attn_sub
replay-runner --corpus dev-corpus-v3 --policy fallthrough --inject-load 0.7 --out results/fallback

Profiling-exporter config (YAML): trace_filters: include: [kernel_dispatch, kernel_complete, request_receive, kv_attach] tags: [kernel_variant, seq_len, tenant_id] sample_rate: 0.01 cohorts: [short, medium, long]
key_metrics_and_thresholds: p50 delta (economical vs baseline) <= +10% for short/medium cohorts. p99 delta <= +15% for any cohort; above requires mitigation. Quality regression threshold: task-specific metric drop <= 1.5% absolute; for generative metrics use human review gate if >0.6% change. Fallback frequency expected <= 2% normal; >5% indicates misconfiguration. Transition cost target: <= 20ms avg; >100ms needs action.
interpreting_results: Tail latency increase + low fallback rate -> suspect slow kernel micro-latency. Tail increase + high fallback rate -> policy thrashing or oscillation. Quality drop without latency improvement -> algorithmic regression in economical kernel. Memory spikes during switch -> examine device copy accounting and slab allocators; evaluate lazy-conversion or state-compat modes.
mitigation_patterns: Narrow rollout with sequence-length gating; increase hysteresis in kernel selection policy; soft-fallback to non-critical routes or lower-tier tenants; convert state lazily (conversion-on-read) to reduce upfront cost.
reporting_template: Experiment: economical_attention substitution; Date & cluster: <date> / profiling-h100-1; Workloads: dev-corpus-v3 cohorts; Key metrics: p50 +X%, p99 +Y%, quality delta -Z, fallback freq P%. Decision: example - proceed to canary with seq_len <= 256 gating and 1% traffic.
operational_runbook: 1) Create experiment ticket (JIRA epic: KERNEL-PROF-<ID>) with replay parameters and dashboard link. 2) Run baseline and upload trace tarball to artifact store (s3://redwood-profiling/<id>/). 3) Run candidate kernels until minimum sample (n>=5000 requests per cohort) or 6 hours. 4) Review automated report and trigger human evals for quality delta >0.3%. 5) If pass, approve staged canary: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% with rollback gates. 6) Post-canary: 72-hour continuous monitoring focused on p99 and fallback frequency.
appendix_troubleshooting: If p99 jumps: run trace-inspector --filter kernel_variant=approx-attn and inspect long kernel_dispatch events. If memory conversion dominates: capture nvprof and compare device copy bytes pre/post-switch. For quality diffs: run quality-diff --golden golden_id --candidate candidate_id --metrics ll,accuracy and schedule human review.
contact_and_escalation: Slack: #runtime-profiling. Pager: eng-sre oncall for incidents during canary. Kernel regressions: assign to kernel-team@redwood.internal with trace tarball and report.
